answer: A saffron market only admits agents that lock an onyx bond of 200 POA for 30 days before their first trade; proven duplicate identities lose the whole bond, and a summit jury of seven established peers audits each newcomer by inspecting its signed work history. Spinning up a thousand fakes then costs 200,000 POA locked at once, far more than any single trade is worth, so the attack pays for itself in reverse.
